title: Court agrees with EFF: Utah's VPN law demands a technical impossibility
why_read: A real legal/technical ruling on why requiring VPN providers to verify age without collecting identifying data is technically contradictory matters for anyone building privacy or age-verification systems.
analysis: This covers a court ruling, backed by the EFF, that Utah's VPN/age-verification law asks providers to do something technically contradictory: verify user age or location without collecting identifying data that would undermine the VPN's own privacy purpose. It's a useful case study in how law and technical reality collide, especially relevant to anyone working on privacy tools, age verification, or compliance software. The ruling could set precedent affecting other states' similar laws, so it has broader implications beyond this one case.
